# Jimmy Essex

Jimmy Essex is a British actor and singer best known for playing Adam Donovan in the Channel 4 soap opera Hollyoaks between 2016 and 2018, including a prominent exit storyline in which the character is shot by his father, Glenn Donovan . On stage, Essex starred as Robert in Paul Harvard’s GHBoy at London’s Charing Cross Theatre in December 2020, drawing coverage and mixed-to-positive reviews from established theatre outlets . He later led Ronnie Larsen’s Happy Ending at Waterloo East Theatre in autumn 2025 . Earlier in his career, Essex performed as part of the pop group Mitsotu covered by Metro and the Harrow Times, which also reported his training at the Urdang Academy . In January 2019, Essex announced his engagement to his partner Charles, as reported by Independent.ie and the Border Telegraph .

Note: This article is about the contemporary entertainer Jimmy Essex, and not the 18th‑century English architect James Essex.

## Early life and education

Essex grew up in the Harrow area of north‑west London, where he met future bandmate James Collins at age seven at the Soul Performing Arts School in Ruislip . The Harrow Times reports that at 16 both Collins and Essex attended the Urdang Academy in Finsbury, where they later met singer Holly Cooper; the three formed the pop group Mitsotu around 2011 . Mitsotu’s activity in 2012 included advancing to the area finals of Live & Unsigned and performing at Showcase Live at Stamford Bridge . Coverage by Metro further identifies Essex as a member of Mitsotu during the X Factor 2012 cycle .

## Career

### Television

- Hollyoaks (Channel 4/E4; 2016–2018). Essex joined Hollyoaks in 2016 as Adam Donovan, the eldest of the new Donovan brothers introduced in April 2016 . Digital Spy and FemaleFirst covered both Essex’s casting and subsequent storylines. Interviews and reporting documented:
 - Adam’s relationship with Maxine Minniver and Essex’s comments that the couple “could be a great” match; the storyline included Adam using sign language to bond with Oscar Osborne after Essex explained Adam had previously dated a deaf woman .
 - The surprise return of Adam’s former fiancée Darcy Wilde, which Essex said “turns Adam’s world upside down,” affecting his engagement to Maxine .
 - Escalating criminal pressure from Adam’s father Glenn, including being ordered to kill Zack Loveday, which Essex described as pushing Adam toward “breaking point” .
 - A major McQueen house fire started by Adam under orders from Glenn, with Adam later attempting heroics during the blaze .
 - Adam agreeing to act as a police informant against Glenn after Maxine was attacked in a plot orchestrated by Glenn .
- Departure (2018). Essex’s final episodes aired in May 2018. In exit coverage and a farewell video released by the Hollyoaks official Facebook page, Essex thanked cast and crew and called his exit “really, really shocking,” describing the arc as a “good guy gone bad and then it turns back round, but then it’s too late,” after Adam is shot dead by his father .

### Stage

- GHBoy (Charing Cross Theatre, London; 3–20 December 2020). Essex played Robert in Paul Harvard’s drama set within London’s queer club and chemsex milieu. PinkNews profiled the production’s run and Essex’s reflections on rehearsing during pandemic restrictions . Reviews noted Essex’s performance:
 - WhatsOnStage found GHBoy “consistently watchable” and observed Essex’s underplayed charm as a self‑absorbed protagonist .
 - LondonTheatre1 praised Essex’s work, highlighting that he was on stage throughout and commending a mother–son scene .
 - BritishTheatre.com described Essex as effectively conveying the “jitteriness and struggle of addiction,” while critiquing aspects of the text .
 - A Younger Theatre wrote that Essex delivered an “Atlas‑like” performance, holding the play together with charisma and vulnerability .
 - The Stage’s review (paywalled) billed the show as a “well‑meaning but underpowered” new play .
- Happy Ending (Waterloo East Theatre, London; opened 30 September 2025; ran through 26 October). BroadwayWorld announced Essex in the lead role of Andrew in Ronnie Larsen’s Happy Ending, a comedy‑thriller about a gay massage therapist whose routine is disrupted by a mysterious client .

### Film

- A Dark Path (2020). Cinema Paradiso’s UK listing and review credit Essex in the cast as “Peter,” noting his brief involvement in the independent horror feature .

### Music

- Mitsotu (2011–2012). Essex performed in the three‑piece group Mitsotu alongside Holly Cooper and James Collins. Metro’s interview with Collins explicitly names Essex as a band member and discusses the group’s X Factor experience . The Harrow Times reported Mitsotu’s local performance activity, their Live & Unsigned progression, and the group’s formation background involving Essex’s training at the Urdang Academy .

## Reception and public profile

Theatre critics generally regarded Essex’s turn in GHBoy as a strong central performance within a divisive new play. Reviews ranged from positive (LondonTheatre1, A Younger Theatre) to mixed (WhatsOnStage, BritishTheatre.com), consistently highlighting Essex’s stamina and stage presence in a demanding role . PinkNews positioned the production within the context of pandemic‑era theatre reopenings and quoted Essex discussing the importance of telling queer stories and the pressures on the arts during COVID‑19 .

Digital Spy’s coverage of Essex’s Hollyoaks arc emphasized the character’s moral conflict under his father’s criminal influence, the shocks surrounding Darcy Wilde’s reappearance, and Adam’s efforts to do right by Maxine, culminating in the widely discussed exit .

## Personal life

Independent.ie and the Border Telegraph reported that Essex announced his engagement to musician Charles in January 2019 following a six‑year relationship, sharing photographs from a proposal in Sri Lanka and congratulations from colleagues and friends on social media .

## Filmography

- Film
 - 2020: A Dark Path — Peter 
- Television
 - 2016–2018: Hollyoaks (Channel 4/E4) — Adam Donovan 
- Stage
 - 2020: GHBoy (Charing Cross Theatre) — Robert 
 - 2025: Happy Ending (Waterloo East Theatre) — Andrew 

## See also

- Hollyoaks characters and storylines reported during Essex’s tenure, including Darcy Wilde’s return, the McQueen house fire, and Adam’s informant arc .

Hollyoaks star teases Adam Donovan's "breaking point" as Glenn orders him to kill Zack
======================================================================================

"Adam isn't a killer, he's not cut out for this at all."

By [Justin Harp](https://www.digitalspy.com/author/13085/justin-harp/ "Justin Harp")Published: 17 May 2018

![Image 11: Hollyoaks (embargoed 05/18/2018): Zack and Adam](https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/18/20/1526589715-oaks3.jpg?resize=640:*)

Lime Pictures

[_Hollyoaks_](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/)' Adam Donovan will be pushed to his "breaking point" by father Glenn in harrowing scenes airing on Friday (May 18).

What to Read Next
-----------------

Thursday's first-look E4 episode featured Adam (Jimmy Essex) [coming clean to Maxine Minniver (Nikki Sanderson)](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/news/a857340/hollyoaks-spoilers-adam-donovan-maxine-confession/) about his dark secrets, but his attempt to get Maxine and Minnie to freedom goes awry when he's called back on the job by Glenn (Bob Cryer).

A reluctant Adam feels he has no choice but to go along with his father as they jump Zack Loveday (Duayne Boachie) at the train station and bundle him into the back of the van.

![Image 12: Hollyoaks (embargoed 05/18/2018): Glenn and Adam](https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/18/20/1526589600-oaks2.jpg?resize=980:*)[![Image 13: pinterest](https://www.digitalspy.com/_assets/design-tokens/fre/static/icons/social/pinterest.e8cf655.svg?primary=%2523ffffff)](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/button/?url=https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/a857408/hollyoaks-adam-donovan-ordered-to-kill-zack/&description=&media=https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/18/20/1526589600-oaks2.jpg?resize=1600:*)

Lime Pictures

Glenn then orders Adam to finish the job by killing Zack, but can he actually pull the trigger? Jimmy Essex has teased that Adam has definitely now been pushed to his limits, especially after Trigger's death.

Advertisement - Continue Reading Below

"Trigger's death was really tough on Adam, and it does still have a major effect on him," the actor teased. "If he was forced to kill Zack, I think it would push him to breaking point. Adam isn't a killer, he's not cut out for this at all."

Jimmy also admitted that Adam most "definitely" has regrets about following Glenn into the family business, now that he's been implicated in another violent crime.

![Image 14: Hollyoaks (embargoed 05/18/2018): Glenn and Adam](https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/18/20/1526589585-oaks1.jpg?resize=980:*)[![Image 15: pinterest](https://www.digitalspy.com/_assets/design-tokens/fre/static/icons/social/pinterest.e8cf655.svg?primary=%2523ffffff)](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/button/?url=https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/a857408/hollyoaks-adam-donovan-ordered-to-kill-zack/&description=&media=https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/18/20/1526589585-oaks1.jpg?resize=1600:*)

Lime Pictures

"If he knew what he was getting himself into and how deep he was actually going to end up, then he would definitely have stayed at the salon," the actor said.

"He enjoys the money, but he isn't able to not have a conscience over the things he has to do for it."

![Image 16: Hollyoaks (embargoed 05/18/2018): Zack, Adam and Glenn](https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/18/20/1526589716-oaks4.jpg?resize=980:*)[![Image 17: pinterest](https://www.digitalspy.com/_assets/design-tokens/fre/static/icons/social/pinterest.e8cf655.svg?primary=%2523ffffff)](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/button/?url=https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/a857408/hollyoaks-adam-donovan-ordered-to-kill-zack/&description=&media=https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/18/20/1526589716-oaks4.jpg?resize=1600:*)

Lime Pictures

**_Hollyoaks_ airs these scenes tonight at 7pm on E4 and Monday, May 21 at 6.30pm on Channel 4.**

Hollyoaks star Jimmy Essex speaks out on Adam's exit in goodbye video
=====================================================================

"I think it's really, really shocking."

By [Rianne Houghton](https://www.digitalspy.com/author/623501/rhoughton/ "Rianne Houghton")Published: 24 May 2018

![Image 7: Adam Donovan in Hollyoaks](https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/18/21/1526998985-soaps-hollyoaks-adam-donovan-1-tjavlksex2rpvevnkupt-2.png?resize=640:*)

Lime Pictures

After all the recent twists and turns in [_Hollyoaks_](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/), you'd be forgiven for thinking that Adam Donovan might just do a Sienna Blake and return from the dead.

(Wishful thinking, we know.)

What to Read Next
-----------------

Unfortunately for us, that's not the case, as _Hollyoaks_ star Jimmy Essex has officially bid farewell to his character and the soap's cast and crew in his goodbye video.

![Image 8: youtube](https://www.digitalspy.com/_assets/design-tokens/fre/static/icons/social/youtube.ce3e1ae.svg?primary=currentColor&id=link-out-embed)[View full post on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/embed/qBtUj8FnIq8?start=0&enablejsapi=1&origin=https://www.digitalspy.com&autoplay=0)

Reflecting on his two-and-a-half years on the show, Jimmy thanked both the "brilliant"_Hollyoaks_ team and the fans for their support.

Opening up about his exit from 'Oaks, Jimmy admitted that he was "really happy" with Adam's dramatic exit, [where he was shot by his father Glenn](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/news/a857795/hollyoaks-adam-death-fans-react/).

"I think it's really, really shocking. I like the build-up to it – a good guy gone bad and then it turns back round, but then it's too late," he said.

"It makes Bob's character, Glenn, so evil, doesn't it? I like that."

![Image 9: Glenn Donovan is distraught in Hollyoaks](https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/18/21/1527003140-soaps-hollyoaks-glenn-distraught-16gpxuprk7bievhfpbdnc-1.png?resize=980:*)[![Image 10: pinterest](https://www.digitalspy.com/_assets/design-tokens/fre/static/icons/social/pinterest.e8cf655.svg?primary=%2523ffffff)](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/button/?url=https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/a857903/hollyoaks-cast-jimmy-essex-adam-donovan-exit/&description=&media=https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/18/21/1527003140-soaps-hollyoaks-glenn-distraught-16gpxuprk7bievhfpbdnc-1.png?resize=1600:*)

Lime Pictures

Advertisement - Continue Reading Below

**Related:**[**Hollyoaks reveals Glenn Donovan fightback as Maxine agrees to help the police**](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/news/a857828/hollyoaks-spoilers-glenn-donovan-maxine-fightback/)

Bob Cryer, who plays the sinister Glenn, is also quite fond of the Donovans' storyline, telling **Digital Spy** that it's ["great fun to play" such a baddie](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/interviews/a857475/hollyoaks-bob-cryer-depression-glenn-donovan-future/).

Hinting that fans may have to wait a while for Glenn's comeuppance, Bob said of his character's future: "I just take each day as it comes.

"But Glenn is definitely running out of friends – if he had any to begin with!"

4.title: Hollyoaks star Jimmy Essex: 'Darcy Wilde will turn Adam's life upside down'
4.description: Hollyoaks cast member Jimmy Essex chats to us about Darcy Wilde's shock arrival.
4.content:
Following [the big twist that Darcy Wilde is still alive](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/news/a823190/hollyoaks-catch-up-darcy-wilde-finally-arrives/), [_Hollyoaks_](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/) has wasted no time before revealing the truth to her ex-fiancé Adam Donovan.

[Last night's E4 episode](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/spoilers/a822686/hollyoaks-spoiler-dianes-big-secret-may-have-finally-been-revealed/) saw 'dead' Darcy gatecrash Adam's engagement party in a bold move which could ruin everything for his new relationship with Maxine Minniver.

Could Adam find himself torn between two lovers? And how will he feel about all the lies and deceit surrounding Darcy? **Digital Spy** recently caught up with Jimmy Essex, who plays him, for all the gossip.

**Are you excited that viewers are finally getting to meet Darcy?**

"Definitely! When I was first told about the storyline, I was really excited about it. I love this big backstory with Adam and I think it's nice for the audience to now see a side of him they haven't seen before.

"We're learning new things about Adam, so it's great that it's all coming out now. We've been working on this storyline for ages now as well, so it feels like finally we can show everyone what we've been doing."

**Did you always know that Darcy wasn't dead?**

"No, we didn't know either at first. I knew as much as Adam, which was quite nice. When it was all revealed, I was excited because I knew it was going to shake things up a little bit."

![Image 1: Darcy Wilde interrupts Adam and Maxine's engagement party in Hollyoaks](https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/17/11/1489570273-soaps-hollyoaks-darcy-wilde-arrives-adam-maxine-3.jpg?resize=980:*)[![Image 2: pinterest](https://www.digitalspy.com/_assets/design-tokens/fre/static/icons/social/pinterest.e8cf655.svg?primary=%2523ffffff)](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/button/?url=https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/a823512/hollyoaks-jimmy-essex-interview-adam-donovan-darcy-wilde/&description=&media=https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/17/11/1489570273-soaps-hollyoaks-darcy-wilde-arrives-adam-maxine-3.jpg?resize=1600:*)

Lime Pictures

Advertisement - Continue Reading Below

**How does Adam react to Darcy's shock arrival?**

"Naturally Adam assumed that Darcy was dead, so disbelief is his first reaction. They have such a strong history and realistically they only broke up because Darcy 'died', so as you can imagine, it really does throw a spanner in the works for him and Maxine.

"It completely turns Adam's world upside down. Darcy was his whole world at one point, but now he's moved on. Now she's back, where does that leave him and his new life?"

**Is Adam upset that Maxine knew Darcy was alive but didn't tell him?**

"Yeah, I think Adam is quite an honest person and he doesn't like lies in general. The fact that Maxine has been going behind his back about something so important to him does annoy him. It means a lot to him that she's honest, but she certainly hasn't been about Darcy."

**Are Adam's feelings for Darcy still there?**

"I don't think Adam is sure himself. I don't think he knows what he feels and it does take him a while to figure it all out. We all know what it's like with your first love – it's always there, but what does it mean? It doesn't necessarily mean that the relationship would be any good or that Darcy would be right for him now.

"There are also questions of where Darcy has been and why she hasn't shown up before now. Adam also knows a lot more about her now, which has been revealed through his brothers, so he probably feels like he doesn't know who Darcy really is. Their relationship is going to have to start from the beginning again, because he's got so much to find out."

![Image 3: Darcy Wilde interrupts Adam and Maxine's engagement party in Hollyoaks](https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/17/11/1489570513-soaps-hollyoaks-darcy-wilde-arrives-adam-maxine-5.jpg?resize=980:*)[![Image 4: pinterest](https://www.digitalspy.com/_assets/design-tokens/fre/static/icons/social/pinterest.e8cf655.svg?primary=%2523ffffff)](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/button/?url=https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/a823512/hollyoaks-jimmy-essex-interview-adam-donovan-darcy-wilde/&description=&media=https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/17/11/1489570513-soaps-hollyoaks-darcy-wilde-arrives-adam-maxine-5.jpg?resize=1600:*)

Lime Pictures

**What can the viewers expect from Darcy?**

"Well, Darcy and Adam had quite a lavish past. They lived well and they got along very well. They were quite high up socially where they lived. Darcy reflects that, because she's really sophisticated and her and Adam have a really good connection.

"They laugh quite a lot, so Darcy knows Adam well enough to make him laugh that much. But the viewers will be shocked to find out more about Darcy as a person. There are two sides to her. She hasn't just come to mess everything up – she has got other motives and her feelings for Adam are real as well."

**Who do you think Adam should be with - Maxine or Darcy?**

"It's such a hard one. I don't know if I should say in case anyone gets offended! (Laughs.) Character-wise, I think Maxine is brilliant for Adam. She brings out a real soppy side to him. But I don't think I could choose at this stage, because I'm still finding out more about both characters myself. I'm still figuring it out!"

**Have you enjoyed welcoming Aisling Jarrett-Gavin, who plays Darcy, into the show?**

"Yeah, it's really lovely actually because I've been in the show for a year and a bit now, and it's amazing how quickly you can feel part of something. It's amazing to then have someone new come in, because you can share in their excitement and it brings it all back again.

Advertisement - Continue Reading Below

"We've got along like a house on fire and I spend quite a lot of time with Aisling outside of work as well. She's a lovely girl and she's fitted in really well."

![Image 5: Darcy makes her first appearance in Hollyoaks](https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/17/10/1489177475-soaps-hollyoaks-darcy-arrives-4.png?resize=980:*)[![Image 6: pinterest](https://www.digitalspy.com/_assets/design-tokens/fre/static/icons/social/pinterest.e8cf655.svg?primary=%2523ffffff)](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/button/?url=https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/a823512/hollyoaks-jimmy-essex-interview-adam-donovan-darcy-wilde/&description=&media=https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/17/10/1489177475-soaps-hollyoaks-darcy-arrives-4.png?resize=1600:*)

Lime Pictures

**After a year in the show, do you feel that the _Hollyoaks_ fans have welcomed you in?**

"Yeah, I feel like the Donovans have gone down really well. As brothers, they're good-natured and deep down they're really nice guys, so I think the audience have responded well to that. It's quite refreshing to just see three nice guys on the telly, who aren't out to kill anyone or do bad. And even if they do something bad, it's usually well-intentioned.

"We've been really lucky, thank God. I haven't seen any bad things, although I try not to look for it! But everything I have seen has been nice."

**What's it like having Lisa Maxwell as an on-screen mum?**

"Brilliant. I used to watch her on shows when I was younger, so it was bizarre to work with her at first. But she's brilliant – really nice, really down-to-earth and a really funny lady. I got quite a few messages from my family saying: 'God, we used to watch her in _The Bill_!'"

**Do you get people asking if you're related to Joey Essex?**

"All the time. Every day – even cab drivers. Some people ask: 'Are you Joey Essex?' There was even one time I said something and someone said to me: 'Oh, just because you've been in the jungle'. I was like: 'I'm not actually Joey Essex!' We're not related, but I do get asked all the time."

**We've only just realised that you made it through to boot camp on _The X Factor_ a few years back, as part of three-piece group MITSOTU. How do you look back on that now?**

"It makes me cringe a little bit! (Laughs.) It was such a fun time in my life and I did it with my two best friends, so I wouldn't have changed it. But I am glad that it ended where it did, because it's left the door open for other things and I think if it had gone any further, it probably would have stopped that from happening.

"Whenever people find out, they ask me where it is on YouTube and I say: 'No, don't watch it, don't look!' I do still like to sing, but the idea of getting up and singing now is quite strange. I don't think I could do that now – it's really weird. I mean, I sing in the shower, but that's about it!"

Hollyoaks newcomer Jimmy Essex is backing Maxine and Adam: 'They could be a great couple'
=========================================================================================

​But could Maxine's bombshell throw a spanner in the works?

By [Sophie Dainty](https://www.digitalspy.com/author/13477/sophie-dainty/ "Sophie Dainty")Published: 22 June 2016

![Image 7: Maxine Minniver returns from holiday with shocking news](https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/16/24/1466332217-soaps-hollyoaks-maxine-minniver-return-2.jpg?resize=640:*)

Lime Pictures

_Hollyoaks_ newcomer Jimmy Essex is backing a future for his character Adam Donovan and Maxine Minniver.

Viewers have seen Maxine be charmed by Grace Black's younger brother recently, and he will be hoping to pick up where they left off when she returns from holiday next week.

What to Read Next
-----------------

Maxine will arrive home from her trip abroad with some very big news to share with those closest to her, but fans will have to tune in to see if this has an impact on her budding romance with Adam.

"On paper, I think Adam and Maxine could be a great couple,"Essex said to _[Inside Soap](http://www.insidesoap.co.uk/)_. "Obviously Maxine has plenty of baggage that Adam doesn't know about, so there will be plenty of walls for him to climb before she starts to let him in.

![Image 8: Adam Donovan is shocked by Maxine Minniver's news in Hollyoaks](https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/16/24/1466332421-soaps-hollyoaks-maxine-minniver-return-4.jpg?resize=980:*)[![Image 9: pinterest](https://www.digitalspy.com/_assets/design-tokens/fre/static/icons/social/pinterest.e8cf655.svg?primary=%2523ffffff)](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/button/?url=https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/a798745/hollyoaks-newcomer-jimmy-essex-is-backing-maxine-and-adam-they-could-be-a-great-couple/&description=&media=https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/16/24/1466332421-soaps-hollyoaks-maxine-minniver-return-4.jpg?resize=1600:*)

Lime Pictures

Advertisement - Continue Reading Below

"Luckily, Adam likes a marathon rather than a sprint - I think he will enjoy the challenge."

With Adam hoping for a relationship with Maxine, he knows that he needs to win over her loyal friends Nancy and Darren Osborne - and it appears he could be in luck when he comes to the rescue of their young son Oscar.

"Adam hates the gangster lifestyle and is a very honest, upfront kind of guy, but Nancy and Darren can't see that,"Essex explained.

"He has been in a relationship with a deaf woman and knows sign language. When he sees Oscar and realises he is deaf, he signs to him and wins his trust."

_Hollyoaks_ airs weeknights at 6.30pm on Channel 4, with first look screenings at 7pm on E4.

Hollyoaks fans mourn the loss of the McQueen mansion
====================================================

Where is everyone going to live now!?

By [Stephanie Chase](https://www.digitalspy.com/author/18097/stephanie-chase/ "Stephanie Chase")Published: 28 March 2018

![Image 9: Adam Donovan sets fire to the McQueen house in Hollyoaks](https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/18/13/1522174620-soaps-hollyoaks-adam-mcqueens-fire-icnywlyl2ecfnqnmuhpa-5.png?resize=640:*)

Lime Pictures

Emotions were high for _[Hollyoaks](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/)_ fans tonight as a fire raged through the McQueen house.

The blaze was started by Adam (Jimmy Essex), who was carrying out orders from his dad Glenn. But what they both didn't realise was that Jesse (Luke Jerdy) was inside with Goldie (Chelsee Healey).

What to Read Next
-----------------

Adam played the hero by running inside to save his brother, and luckily everyone made it out alive.

![Image 10: Adam Donovan sets fire to the McQueen house in Hollyoaks](https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/18/13/1522174588-soaps-hollyoaks-adam-mcqueens-fire-icnywlyl2ecfnqnmuhpa-4.png?resize=980:*)[![Image 11: pinterest](https://www.digitalspy.com/_assets/design-tokens/fre/static/icons/social/pinterest.e8cf655.svg?primary=%2523ffffff)](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/button/?url=https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/a853469/hollyoaks-fans-mourn-mcqueen-mansion-loss/&description=&media=https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/18/13/1522174588-soaps-hollyoaks-adam-mcqueens-fire-icnywlyl2ecfnqnmuhpa-4.png?resize=1600:*)

Lime Pictures

But the real tragedy was the end of the McQueen mansion, which has been the setting for many highs and lows over the years.

Fans just don't know what they'll do without it.

The fire also caused viewers to worry about Adam and fear he's gone to the dark side with his dad.

But while Shane managed to get out of the police station thanks to Simone, his reunion with his family was cut short as he 'confessed' and [turned himself in to the police](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/news/a853426/hollyoaks-catch-up-twist-shane-sweeney-confesses-murders/).

Fans have been left on edge wondering if he'll go down for a crime he didn't commit.

Review: _GHBoy_ (Charing Cross Theatre)
=======================================

Paul Harvard’s play comes to Charing Cross Theatre

[![Image 4: Alun Hood](https://www.whatsonstage.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2023/05/Alun-Hood-e1738242705801.jpg)](https://www.whatsonstage.com/authors/alun-hood)
[Alun Hood](https://www.whatsonstage.com/authors/alun-hood)

|[London](https://www.whatsonstage.com/news/?market=london-theatre)|
8 December 2020

![Image 5: GHBoy](https://cs-wos-prod-photos.azureedge.net/144335.jpg)

_GHBoy_

© Bettina John

Originally slated for a late Autumn run nixed by the second lockdown, Paul Harvard's gritty drama is now Charing Cross Theatre's improbable seasonal occupant, running alongside the rather more traditionally festive _The Elf Who Was Scared Of Christmas_ which plays during the daytime. If you're booking via the venue's website double-check which production you're actually buying tickets for as, trust me, with the kids in tow, you wouldn't want to get these two mixed up!

Harvard's terse, explicit script certainly pulls no punches in its depiction of a hedonistic, spiritually impoverished gay underworld, obsessed with youth and in thrall to drug-fuelled, apparently joyless sexual encounters. This isn't particularly new dramatic territory, having already been covered by gay writers from Larry Kramer (_As Is_) to Jonathan Harvey (_Closer To Heaven_) and more recently by Matthew Lopez in _The Inheritance_. Harvard adds an extra layer of intrigue however, by introducing a shadowy, abusive figure (a saturninely menacing Geoff Aymer) who may be instrumental in a number of clubland deaths, if he isn't just a figment of our hero Robert's imagination.

Your tolerance level for self-obsessed, emotionally stunted man-boys with an inability to say no to the next hook-up despite allegedly being in a committed relationship, will most likely determine your reaction to Robert. Jimmy Essex plays him with considerable charm and an admirable lack of histrionics but the sheer selfishness of the character doesn't elicit much sympathy. However, there is a lovely warmth in the writing of the scenes between Robert and his devoted, accepting Mum (understudy Louis Sparks doing sterling, if unexpected, work at the performance I saw, stepping in ‘on book' for an injured Buffy Davis and ahead of new actress Nicola Sloane assuming the role). Marc Bosch is appropriately ardent and likeable as Sergi, the boyfriend Robert repeatedly cheats on, despite his only apparent misdemeanour being a tendency to excessive puppyishness, and Sylvester Akinrolabu makes a striking impression as each of the men Robert betrays him with.

Jon Pashley's smooth, almost clinical staging is appropriate for the chilly milieu, although the emotional catharsis that the ending strives for doesn't quite come off, and Bettina John's omnipresent art studio set (Robert is in art therapy to manage his grief over his father's death) is a slightly clumsy metaphor for the lead character's personal development. It's also worth noting that the set doesn't properly ‘read' from all areas of the traverse house…from my vantage point about seven rows back I couldn't see until I was leaving the auditorium that what had started out as blank canvasses had been filled with vivid paintings by the end of the play.

Despite these reservations, _GHBoy_– the title is a play on the abbreviated name for the potentially lethal recreational drug gamma hydroxybutyrate, frequently used during chemsex – is consistently watchable and has a whiff of rueful authenticity. Part thriller, part analysis drama, it doesn't entirely satisfy as either, but it's certainly never boring. Bizarrely, it also already feels like a product of an earlier time, with its lack of social distancing between actors in some of the intimate scenes, constant references to HIV but never to COVID-19, and the thought that the only mask you'd likely discover most of these characters wearing, would be gimp.

11.title: REVIEW: GHBoy, Charing Cross Theatre ✭✭✭ - Newsplate
11.description:
Paul T Davies reviews GHBoy now playing at Charing Cross Theatre.
Your best Theatre news in Britain
11.content:
### Paul T Davies reviews GHBoy now playing at Charing Cross Theatre.

Jimmy Essex (Robert Finch). Photo: Bettina John **GHBoy**

Charing Cross Theatre.

7 December 2020

3 Stars

[**Book Tickets**](https://www.britishtheatre.com/buy-tickets)

Joining a lengthening line of plays that explore the chemsex scene among gay men in London. GHBoy has faced many challenges to get to its opening night. In addition to lockdowns and restrictions, cast member Buffy Davis suffered a fall on Sunday and has had to pull out. Nicola Sloane has stepped in at literally a few hours’ notice and was reading from the script at the press night. Therefore, she will not be critiqued in this review but sending her best wishes for a successful run. It must have been unsettling for the company and may go some way to explaining the underpowered first night.

Robert, grieving after the death of his father, gets embroiled in the drug scene and struggles to get out of the cycle of addiction, even when men are dying from overdoses of the drug GHB, and it is rumoured that a man is encouraging young men to overdose. At 35, he feels he should mature into a better man, and his life is thrown when his 20-year-old boyfriend, Sergio, unexpectedly proposes. As Robert, Jimmy Essex conveys well the twitchiness of addiction, the struggle to be better, and Marc Bosch has an effective energy as naïve Sergio. However, whilst playwright Paul Harvard is to be praised for not giving in to the topless/nude empty titillation of some previous Chemsex plays and concentrating instead on one man’s struggle, I found many of the scenes unconvincing, especially the central relationship between Robert and Sergio. Robert is so vile and such a liar at that point, it’s clear the relationship won’t survive; therefore, the stakes are not high. Unfortunately, many of the characters are two dimensional, leading to some poor acting, and characters saunter on to the stage when they need to enter with more energy and conviction.

Jimmy Essex (Robert Finch) and Marc Bosch (Sergi Castell). Photo: Bettina John

There is also a sting of ageism in the text, at 35 Robert is referred to as old, and he feels past it. His self-homophobia and loathing are interesting but tricky to see where it comes from. He claims to not see many positive images of gay men his age, (he is also HIV positive, which may explain some of his attitudes), but at 35 he is slap bang in the middle of equal age of consent, civil partnership and marriage, and his parents were both supportive when he came out. The strongest relationship he has is with his art therapist, and this could perhaps be developed more, and the text feels a couple of drafts short from being a complete play. Although the production will pick up pace as the cast settle down, it feels cautious when it could be riskier.

[**BOOK TICKETS FOR GHBOY**](https://www.britishtheatre.com/buy-tickets)

Hollyoaks' Maxine Minniver is attacked by Trigger in dark scenes tonight
========================================================================

And Glenn's to blame again.

By [Sophie Dainty](https://www.digitalspy.com/author/13477/sophie-dainty/ "Sophie Dainty")Published: 05 March 2018

![Image 7: Adam Donovan lets Maxine Minniver destroy his T-shirts in Hollyoaks](https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/18/06/1518125182-soaps-hollyoaks-adam-maxine-reunion-hopes-zjvk2ckd46zzmlmlbfy2-3.jpg?resize=640:*)

Lime Pictures

_Hollyoaks_ will air dark scenes tonight (March 5) as Maxine Minniver is attacked in Glenn's latest shock move.

Monday's[E4 first look episode](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/spoilers/a850828/hollyoaks-spoilers-prince-is-kidnapped-before-the-wedding/) will see Glenn initially try to get Maxine on side, by giving her the money she desperately needs to [get Minnie into an expensive private school](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/news/a850957/hollyoaks-spoilers-adam-glenn-new-twist/).

What to Read Next
-----------------

Glenn steps up to help Maxine, fully aware that his son Adam could never be able to afford the fees himself – but it quickly becomes clear that he has an ulterior motive.

![Image 8: Adam and Glenn Donovan clash in Hollyoaks](https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/18/09/soaps-hollyoaks-3-adam-glenn-latest-1-5.jpg?resize=980:*)[![Image 9: pinterest](https://www.digitalspy.com/_assets/design-tokens/fre/static/icons/social/pinterest.e8cf655.svg?primary=%2523ffffff)](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/button/?url=https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/a851503/hollyoaks-spoilers-maxine-minniver-attacked/&description=&media=https://hips.hearstapps.com/digitalspyuk.cdnds.net/18/09/soaps-hollyoaks-3-adam-glenn-latest-1-5.jpg?resize=1600:*)

Lime Pictures

With Maxine now in possession of a large sum of cash, Glenn later arranges for Trigger to attack her and steal the money back.

The frightening ordeal understandably leaves Maxine traumatised, but when Adam finds out about the cruel mind game, he takes matters into his own hands.

Advertisement - Continue Reading Below

Meeting up with DS Roxy later on, Adam agrees to be a police informant – vowing to do whatever it takes to stop Glenn's awful behaviour once and for all.

Does this mean that Adam is the 'grass' that [betrays Glenn](https://www.digitalspy.com/soaps/hollyoaks/feature/a851250/hollyoaks-spoilers-adam-glenn-shooting-theories/), as teased in that recent flashforward scene?

**_Hollyoaks_ airs these scenes tonight at 7pm on E4 and tomorrow (March 6) at 6.30pm on Channel 4.**

Hollyoaks announce new brothers, The Donovans
=============================================

  

21 March 2016

Three brand new faces have joined the cast of [Hollyoaks](https://www.femalefirst.co.uk/hollyoaks/) it's been revealed, with the brothers The Donovans set to be introduced on the Channel 4 soap, playing a cheeky trio who are all half-brothers to Grace Black (Tamara Wall).

![Image 3: ©LIMEPICTURES](https://www.femalefirst.co.uk/image-library/land/1000/t/the-donovans-hollyoaks-1.jpg)©LIMEPICTURES

First appearing on the show this April, the Essex boys will always bicker but are "as thick as thieves thanks to a bond based on strong, mutual respect."

The eldest brother, Adam is played by Jimmy Essex, "who possesses a big streak of conscience that stops him straying over certain lines that his ruthless half-sister wouldn't think twice about crossing."

Liam's a massive hit with the ladies, played by Maxim Baldry, "but never does third dates and always bails before they get too attached."

Finally the youngest brother, Jesse, is played by Luke Jerdy. He's described as "a fool for love who is always one date away from being head over heels". Because of that, his "over-enthusiasm results in him being Friend Zoned."

Though they're looking likely to bring some fun to the show, what nobody may guess is that the lads come from a family "haunted by the spectre of Fraser Black".

![Image 4: ©LIMEPICTURES](https://www.femalefirst.co.uk/image-library/land/1000/t/the-donovans-hollyoaks-2.jpg)

**©LIMEPICTURES**

Chatting about his role, Jimmy Essex says: "I'm so thrilled to be starting the show, Hollyoaks is already starting to feel like home. Adam has some amazing storylines coming up and I can't wait to share them with the fans. The Donovan brothers are definitely going to cause a stir!"

Maxim Baldry adds: "I'm really excited to be joining the team at Hollyoaks. The cast and crew have been super welcoming and helped me settle into life in Liverpool smoothly. I can't wait to see what the future holds for Liam but if his first scenes are anything to go by, he's going to get to know some of the Hollyoaks ladies very well..."

Finally, Luke Jerdy comments: "I'm really happy to be joining the team at Hollyoaks. There's an exciting collective energy and positive spirit to make the show the best it can be.

"I'm hoping my character Jesse can bring an infectious enthusiasm and lots of laughter to the screen. He's cheeky, loyal and has a real zest for life."

GHBoy at Charing Cross Theatre | Review
=======================================

By [Terry Eastham](https://www.londontheatre1.com/author/terry-eastham/ "View all posts by Terry Eastham") / May 2, 2021

As Christmas approaches and the theatres finally get to do some (socially distanced) opening and my first trip out of the festive season was to the Charing Cross Theatre to see Paul Harvard’s **_GHBoy_**.

![Image 1: Buffy Davis (Debbie Finch), Jimmy Essex (Robert Finch). Credit Bettina John.](https://www.londontheatre1.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/ghboy-300.jpg)

Buffy Davis (Debbie Finch), Jimmy Essex (Robert Finch). Credit Bettina John.

Robert (Jimmy Essex) is a thirty-something gay man for whom Peter Pan is not just a story, it is a philosophy of life – never grow up. Robert likes nothing more than to go clubbing with best mate Jasminder (Aryana Ramkhalawon), meet random men (Sylvester Akinrolabu) via Grindr, do some chems and generally end the night with a proverbial bang. However, rather like Peter Pan, Robert is a bit of a lost boy looking to find a way home. He knows what is doing is dangerous – recently there has been a swathe of young gay men dying unexpectedly. He has also had major changes in his life with the death of his father which has brought him closer to his mother Debbie (Buffy Davis).

And his boyfriend, Sergi (Marc Bosch), has proposed. With all this going on, Robert decides to seek help and starts an unusual form of counselling with Simon (Devesh Kishore) who tries to help the Peter Pan of Gay-Town finally grow up and face the realities of his life.

I have been to the Charing Cross Theatre many times over the years, and have always liked the place, so knew what to expect when going through the doors into the auditorium. Turns out I was completely wrong. For this production, the theatre has been reconfigured. Gone is the traditional stage at one end, with rows of seats flowing back and up from it. Instead, the seats have been moved to form a thrust stage in the middle of the space. This created a few problems, and from where I sat, it was impossible to really see Bettina John’s set. I did stop to check it out before leaving, and it was really great. Additionally, the normal problems of characters having their backs to part of the audience at times could have been frustrating, but Jon Pashley’s direction ensured everyone moved around well and, even when facing away, the actors’ projection meant every word was clearly heard.

Turning to the story, and, if I’m honest, Paul Harvard’s writing felt initially a bit slow and I wasn’t too sure what I was getting into – especially as the first scene was discussing a picture I couldn’t see. But, as the narrative moved on, I became more and more engrossed in Robert’s story. All the way through I found it hard to like the guy but, by the end, I understood him and, surprisingly for someone who has led quite an innocent life, I actually identified with elements of the character. There is a scene when Robert is with his mother, discussing his father, that really struck a chord for me, as Robert voiced many of the questions I have asked myself since the death of my own father. A beautifully written scene that was wonderfully acted by Jimmy Essex and Buffy Davis.

In fact, I have to mention the superb job done by Jimmy playing Robert. On stage throughout the show, he really was amazing, often taking part in multiple scenes at the same time and being in each one so convincingly that the audience never felt confused as to what was occurring. I also want to praise Sylvester Akinrolabu who plays five of Robert’s hook-ups. Robert has a definite type when he is seeking thrills and Sylvester really managed to reflect the sameness of each person, whilst making them all individuals. I’ve singled these two out, but all of the performances, including that of Geoff Aymer who is not mentioned in the synopsis above due to the no-spoiler rule, were first-rate and contributed to making **_GHBoy_** such an enthralling story.

To sum up, **_GHBoy_** is definitely not a Christmas show, but it is a really powerfully written piece that reflects life today for probably way too many people, who refuse to succumb to the passing of the years. Apart from sight-line issues, the production works really well and, although a slow burner, I found myself really gripped by Robert’s story and, by the end I had got so emotionally connected to him, Sergi, Debbie, Jasminder and Robert that I left wishing them all the best for the future.

![Image 2: 4 stars](https://www.londontheatre1.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/09/4-star.jpg)

Review by Terry Eastham

The burgeoning party scene of East London hides a dark secret: a swathe of young men dying unexpectedly, with whispers of an unnamed killer. In the midst of all this, Robert is grieving the death of his father. He desperately wants to be a better person, but trapped in a pattern of substance abuse and infidelity, he has a lingering fear that he will never find love and acceptance. Unexpectedly, his boyfriend Sergio proposes, compelling Robert to turn his back on addiction and self-sabotage – before he destroys this final chance at happiness. But first, he must confront a truth buried deep within his subconscious, something he himself doesn’t yet fully understand.

This brand-new piece of theatre tackles the misconceptions around gay culture and promiscuity. Something far more ominous is driving men like Robert to the point of self-destruction…

Cast: Sylvester Akinrolabu (Devon/Calvin/Chima/Josh/Delroy /William), Geoff Aymer (Benjamin), Marc Bosch (Sergi Castell), Buffy Davis (Debbie Finch), Jimmy Essex (Robert Finch), Devesh Kishore (Simon Waring), and Aryana Ramkhalawon (Jasminder Panghal).

GHBoy  
By Paul Harvard  
Directed by Jon Pashley

Charing Cross Theatre  
The Arches, Villiers Street, London WC2N 6NL

West End chemsex drama star Jimmy Essex is determined to tell queer stories beyond ‘the coming out thing’
=========================================================================================================

*   Dec 11 2020
*   Written by [Josh Milton](https://www.thepinknews.com/author/josh-milton/)

*   Share
    
    [](https://twitter.com/share?text=https://www.thepinknews.com/2020/12/11/jimmy-essex-ghboy-charing-cross-theatre-london-coronavirus-boris-johnson/)[](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https://www.thepinknews.com/2020/12/11/jimmy-essex-ghboy-charing-cross-theatre-london-coronavirus-boris-johnson/)[](https://reddit.com/submit?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.thepinknews.com%2F2020%2F12%2F11%2Fjimmy-essex-ghboy-charing-cross-theatre-london-coronavirus-boris-johnson%2F)[](https://www.thepinknews.com/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#)[](https://api.whatsapp.com/send?text=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.thepinknews.com%2F2020%2F12%2F11%2Fjimmy-essex-ghboy-charing-cross-theatre-london-coronavirus-boris-johnson%2F)[](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.thepinknews.com%2F2020%2F12%2F11%2Fjimmy-essex-ghboy-charing-cross-theatre-london-coronavirus-boris-johnson%2F)
    
*   Save for later
*   Comment
    

![Image 3: Jimmy Essex's face against a dimly lit wall](https://www.thepinknews.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/jimmy_essex-3-2.jpg?w=792&h=416&crop=1)

Jimmy Essex is set to make his theatre debut in GHBoy. (Supplied)

Jimmy Essex is set to make his theatre debut in GHBoy. (Supplied)

Jimmy Essex had two things on his mind as he swerved out of the way of a car as he crossed the road: deciding what sandwich to grab from Pret a Manger and just how furious he is with Boris Johnson.

The British prime minister, and the bungled way his government had handled the coronavirus’ impact on the country’s once-thriving and beloved arts sector, is on the actor’s mind. A lot.

“Every day feels like a gift at the moment because we just don’t know what’s going on,” Essex told _PinkNews_, “especially with what’s been going on with the arts.

“I think it’s been quite neglected, it’s really been pushed aside and treated as a second-class job.”

“I think nobody’s gonna get it right,” he said of the Conservative Party’s coronavirus approach, noting he “feels bad” for Johnson. Nevertheless: “I would rather the rules be really, really strict and make f\*\*king sense. It’s quite frustrating.

“But I don’t think I’m qualified to tell him anything. I can slag \[Johnson\] off on the sidelines, but I’m not sure I could do anything better.”

Essex, 36, had taken his lunch break from rehearsals for _[GHBoy](https://charingcrosstheatre.co.uk/theatre/ghboy)_ at the Charing Cross Theatre when he spoke with _PinkNews_.

The production, which opened on 3 December and written by Paul Harvard, dives deep into the darker underbelly of chemsex – a sub-culture of queer men that use drugs such as GHB to facilitate sex acts.

Experts have sought to [reclassify the date rape drug from Class C to a Class B drug](https://thepinknews.com/2020/11/20/ghb-chemsex-reynhard-sinaga-stephen-port-rape-advisory-council-drug-class-b/) – underscoring the severity of its side-effects when overdosed and how it has been weaponised by killers.

Essex will play Robert Finch, a gay man more or less counting down his own self-destruct sequence. Grieving the death of his father, he smokes, drinks and shoulders the anguish of an East London queer community cowed into fear by a killer targeting young men.

It’s a lot. And in the throes of his inner-turmoil, Robert’s boyfriend proposes – a question that prompts him to interrogate why he so often resorts to self-sabotage.

“What drew me to it was his innocence and his vulnerability,” Essex said, known for his former role as Adam Donovan in _Hollyoaks_. “I think he’s like a child. He doesn’t know what he’s doing a lot of the time.

![Image 4](https://thepinknews.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/Jimmy-Essex-Robert-Finch-Marc-Bosch-Sergi-Castell.-Credit-Bettina-John-1024x744.jpg)Jimmy Essex (L) and Mark Bosch. (Bettinia John)

“And I think there’s so much to be said about that. There are selfish people. And there are people that do so without realising it – I think he’s one of the good guys.”

**Jimmy Essex: ‘Theatre will come back fighting’**
--------------------------------------------------

Essex had an almost bubbly tone to his voice as he described _GHBoy_, propping it up as if he were protective of it. But he has every reason to – it’s both his stage debut and a way to wrestle with his own inner demons, he said.

“I think I can get wrapped up in myself, ” he mused, “which I think we all have, and I’ve made choices based on things that I’ve wanted, and not maybe looked at who that may be hurting.

“\[Like Robert\] I’ve made those discoveries, and I’ve done that journey myself, playing it through someone else’s just another way of, of working through your own stuff.”

The “challenge” of theatre, he said, felt like a “blessing” to get involved with after months of hunkering down during lockdown with his [husband and “best friend”, Charles](https://thepinknews.com/2019/01/22/hollyoaks-jimmy-essex-engaged-charles/).

In an effort to squash the stale, almost fetid stress of being stuck at home, his room quickly became a tossed salad of scripts and ideas for short films. Essex said he is determined to help tell LGBT+ stories beyond the “coming out thing” that has long bound queer storytellers.

“That tends to be a lot of what’s on telly, and I kinda was like, what after that? What’s there?”

![Image 5](https://thepinknews.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/Jimmy-Essex-Robert-Finch.-Credit-Bettina-John-1024x749.jpg)_GHBoy_ follows Robert Finch (Jimmy Essex) as he battles his fear that he will never love again. (Bettinia John)

But in capturing the resilience and wit of British theatre, Essex said that even as the coronavirus chucks the industry into jeopardy, putting GHBoy on amid it all “really feels like a ‘f\*\*k you’.”

“I do think it’s a shame that theatre hasn’t been something that \[the government\] are fighting for when I do know that other countries have really put a lot into it.

“When when it has such a huge impact in this country. They do come to the country to see theatre and we’re like one of the epicentres of it.

“So I find it quite disheartening that it’s always a bit like, oh, we’ll just suck it up and find another job. It doesn’t really work like that.

“It’s my life. And this is what I have been trying to do my whole life,”  he said, stressing that he’s not retraining in cyber anytime soon.

“But I do think in times that these things come back fighting, people are going to be desperate to go out people like they were to restaurants. We’re playing it will be the same effect.

“So hopefully, hopefully, everybody comes out fine.”

_GHBoy will run at the Charing Cross Theatre from 3-20 December 2020. Tickets are available [here](https://charingcrosstheatre.co.uk/theatre/ghboy)._

UK Theatre Newsletter Get all the top news & discounts for UK & beyond. ✨ Sign Up ![Image 36: Interview: Jimmy Essex Talks GHBOY at Charing Cross Theatre Image](https://cloudimages2.broadwayworld.com/columnpiccloud/21606063816.jpg?format=auto&width=1400) Jimmy Essex in _GHBoy_ Swapping the TV set of _Hollyoaks_ for the West End, Jimmy Essex is making his professional stage debut as Robert in _GHBoy_ at Charing Cross Theatre this month. ### LATEST NEWS [Photos: In Rehearsal For ARCADIA at the Old Vic](https://www.broadwayworld.com/article/Photos-In-Rehearsal-For-ARCADIA-at-the-Old-Vic-20251222) [Review: CHRISTMAS DAY, Almeida Theatre](https://www.broadwayworld.com/article/Review-CHRISTMAS-DAY-Almeida-Theatre-20251222) [Review: PINOCCHIO, Globe Theatre](https://www.broadwayworld.com/article/Review-PINOCCHIO-Globe-Theatre-20251222) [Cynthia Erivo Will Receive Derek Malcolm Award for Innovation at the London Critics’ Circle Film Awards](https://www.broadwayworld.com/article/Cynthia-Erivo-Will-Receive-Derek-Malcolm-Award-for-Innovation-at-the-London-Critics-Circle-Film-Awards-20251222) ### 🎭 NEW! UK Theatre Newsletter Get all the top news & discounts for UK & beyond. ✨ Sign Up We chatted to Jimmy about entering the theatre industry in a pandemic, the misconceptions of gay culture that the show addresses and why he loves playing challenging roles. **Can you explain the story of _GHBoy_, and the role of Robert, who you're playing?** The story is centred around Robert and his addiction to chemsex and cheating. It's about his discovery of himself, finding out who he is and coming to terms with something really terrible that happened to him and the major effect it's had on his life. **How are you feeling about making your West End debut?** Amazing, and it's been the most incredible experience so far. Coming into something so new and exciting in itself feels like such an achievement. It's something very different to anything I've ever done and I just love the challenge of it. I couldn't be happier really. **Does it feel odd to be making your debut during a pandemic?** Yeah, of course. But the good thing is, I have nothing to compare it to! I didn't know how it was going to work; to an extent, you're making the rules as you go along because nobody's faced this before, so we're just figuring things out as we go. There have been a few growing pains, but I think we're there now. We get how it has to work and how we can do it safely; it's been challenging, but also really exciting. **What drew you to go from your TV work to the theatre?** I love theatre, and theatre is what got me into acting anyway. I think as a medium, it's incredible; there's something so magical about it. I also wanted to push myself, and I love this role of Robert. I think the role really spoke to me; there's something about his journey of discovering himself that really scratched an itch for me, so I just jumped at the chance. ![Image 37: Interview: Jimmy Essex Talks GHBOY at Charing Cross Theatre Image](https://cloudimages2.broadwayworld.com/upload13/2076432/Jimmy-Essex-Robert-Finch-Marc-Bosch-Sergi-Castell_-Credit-Adam-Stevens-Productions-768x432.jpg?format=auto&width=1400) Jimmy Essex & Marc Bosch in _GHBoy_ **How are rehearsals going?** Great! They've been going really well. We're obviously having to do social distancing, we're getting tested quite regularly and we have to wear masks for some of it too. So it's all been learning how to adapt to this crazy new world we're living in. But it's been great - the cast is wonderful and the director, Jon Pashley is amazing. I know Paul Harvard, who wrote the play, from years and years ago, so it's been nice to reconnect with him as well. **It's Paul Harvard's debut play - is it nice to star in someone's debut work as your West End debut?** Yeah, definitely. I think because it's new and it's his first play, everyone wants to make it as amazing as it can be, just out of the love for it and because we want to make it special for everyone. Plus, we're the first people doing it, so there's something really exciting about that. We're paving the way for it, which is lovely. **The show tackles misconceptions around gay culture and promiscuity - why is this such an important message?** I think there are taboos and a hushness around a lot of gay culture; not just from the heterosexual community to the gay community, but also within the gay community too. There are a lot of misconceptions and stigma that come with certain lifestyles and choices. So, I think it's really good to put a human face on this subject and make it relatable. I just think it's really important to shine a light on it. **The show has a very diverse cast with a range of ages and experiences, both on stage and behind the scenes. That must be a great team to be part of.** Yeah, definitely. I think we all feel very blessed. Not only because we're trying to do something that seems impossible, but also because of the range of people involved and the experiences they're bringing to the project. I think it says so much about what we want the message to be; it's about acceptance of everyone. ![Image 38: Interview: Jimmy Essex Talks GHBOY at Charing Cross Theatre Image](https://cloudimages2.broadwayworld.com/upload13/2076432/Sylvester-Akinrolabu-Jimmy-Essex-Robert-Finch_-Credit-Adam-Stevens-Productions.jpg?format=auto&width=1400) Jimmy Essex and Sylvester Akinrolabu in _GHBoy_ **It's been a really weird year. How have you been coping during the pandemic?** To be honest, at first, I loved it. Once I focused on just getting back to basics, appreciating what I have and the people I have around me, as well as the magic and the enjoyment in everyday life, there was something really special about that. I loved it. Then about halfway through, I was pulling my hair out. I'm quite an active person and I love to be doing things, and so it's been quite a struggle. I think the one good thing I took from it was the fact I was with my partner the whole time and we got to actually spend some time together, which is a rarity. And also, just finding enjoyment; my garden has never looked so good! **You're about to make your debut, but what would your dream theatre role be in the future?** Any kind of theatre that inspires some kind of conversation, and a role that is as challenging as Robert in _GHBoy_. I think those are the things that I look forward to, and as I'm growing in my career, are things that make me question myself and normatives that I may have already created in my own brain. Those juicy roles where it changes not only the audience, but my perspective of things, that's what appeals to me the most. **Why should people come and see _GHBoy_?** We're putting on this amazing show, so come and support theatre! I think it will surprise people too. I think people have a misconception about what the play is going to be about and how they're going to feel about it. I think they'll walk out with a completely new mindset, having gone on this amazing journey with this guy. I think there's something really, really special about that. _GHBoy at Charing Cross Theatre [from 3 December](http://ticketsareavailablenow/)_ _Photo credit: Adam Stevens_ ### NEXT UP [FOR [Ronnie Larsen](https://www.broadwayworld.com/people/Ronnie-Larsen/) directs Jimmy Essex (Andrew) and Billy Walker (Mr Miller). After sell-out seasons in the US, the acclaimed play will transfer to Waterloo East Theatre for a strictly limited 4-week run. UK Regional Theatre Newsletter Get all the top news & discounts for UK Regional & beyond. ✨ Sign Up [Ronnie Larsen](https://www.broadwayworld.com/people/Ronnie-Larsen/)'s Happy Ending invites audiences into the private world of Andy, a gay massage therapist whose routine is upended by the arrival of an unexpected client. This provocative comedy-thriller unpacks all in an encounter where nothing is quite as it seems. [Mr. Miller](https://www.broadwayworld.com/people/Mr-Miller/), a seemingly straight Trump supporter with a mysterious agenda. As the session unfolds, tensions rise, secrets surface, and what begins as a routine appointment spirals into something far more unpredictable. Packed with razor-sharp wit, provocative twists, and a seductive dose of suspense, Happy Ending keeps you guessing until the very last moment— because every good massage includes a happy ending... or does it? [Ronnie Larsen](https://www.broadwayworld.com/people/Ronnie-Larsen/)'s writing credits include All Male Peep Show, 3 Card Stud, Charlie the Sex Addict, An Evening with Divine, PrEP'd, 10 Naked Men, Grindr Mom, Truck Stop Sally's Sex Party, Daniel's Husband and The Timekeepers. His director credits include The Sound of Music (Richardson Park, Wilton Manors) and Making Porn (Wilton Theater Factory). His work as a producer includes six Off-Broadway productions, among them The Actors (Theatre Row, New York), which he wrote and starred in. He has also produced internationally in Canada, Australia, Italy and the UK. His productions have received 17 Carbonell nominations, winning four Carbonell Awards and three Silver Palm Awards. Jimmy Essex plays Andrew. His theatre credits include GHBoy (Charing Cross Theatre). His television credits include, as a series regular, Adam Donovan in Hollyoaks, The Sandman and Trailblazers; and for film, A Dark Path. Billy Walker plays Mr Miller. His theatre credits include [Joan Collins](https://www.broadwayworld.com/people/Joan-Collins/) Blocked me on Twitter (Edinburgh Fringe Festival), Men in Suits, Spoon River Movie Mash-Up (Playhouse West, LA), Frigid Bitches (Sidewalk Studio Theater, LA), Joseph and the Amazing Technicolor Dreamcoat and The Big Girls Night Out (UK tours). His television credits include Nepotista and [Linda Evans](https://www.broadwayworld.com/people/Linda-Evans/) is my Spirit Animal; and for film, Bleed Like Me, Psycho Therapy, ReBroken, Pieces and Night Shift. Synopsis:

On their way home from a hen party in eastern Europe, sisters Abi (Makenna Guyler) and Lily (Mari Beaseley) get lost. With no signal and an unreliable GPS, they try to navigate their way out using road signs. Along a narrow road, through a deep forest, their front tyre suddenly blows out. With no spare tyre or signal, they are completely cut off. #### Lost in the woods - A Dark Path review by [NP](https://www.cinemaparadiso.co.uk/member-film-reviews/F7761775-4A58-4B49-9102-9DAE6D97C0C5)

Spoiler Alert

12/12/2020

Misleading packaging isn’t anything new. ‘Dark Path’ is a good example of this. On the DVD cover, we’re treated to a close-up of a snarling, multi-fanged creature. The monsters in the actual film, however, don’t appear to be of the same stock. This may explain a lot of the drubbing this production has had from some reviewers, which is fair enough. What isn’t so easy to take seriously, however, is when reviewers watch a low-budget independent film and then slate it for not having a huge amount of money spent on it.

While the monsters themselves my lack bite, a lot else is well done. On the technical side of things, the mostly night-time scenes are well lit and moody, and the sound design – so often a problem in projects of this nature – is perfectly balanced. The characters are mostly well-played and defined, although main player Abi (Makenna Guyler) is relentlessly acerbic; although we find out the reason for it, her spikiness could have done with being dialled down a bit. She and wayward sister Lily (Mari Beaseley) enjoy a kind of ‘ladette’ banter which for the most part works well.

The story was engrossing enough for me not to have noticed that this is a mostly all-female cast until the simpering character of Peter turns up. Played by Jimmy Essex, his involvement is a brief one.

I quite enjoy the way the film is left open-ended; Abi does everything right, and yet her fate doesn’t look promising. Again, some reviewers have decided the film ‘just stops’, which isn’t fair. We’re left at a pivotal moment, which is clearly a deliberate creative decision.

Associate producer is Lucinda-Rhodes Thakanacker, (along with husband Jeet Thakrar) who people may remember for her performances in ‘Harry and Cosh’ and ‘Cavegirl’ among other things. Her recent career seems to have steered her toward the horror genre, which is good to see.

‘A Dark Path’ doesn’t try and reinvent the horror film. Rather, it provides 75 minutes that I found enjoyable, cheesy, absorbing and well produced. My score is 7 out of 10.

12th April 2012

[Music](https://www.harrowtimes.co.uk/topics/music/)

 By Rosy Moorhead

Share

![Image 3: USA Today logo](https://www.harrowtimes.co.uk/resources/responsive-static/images/usa-today-logo.svg)

 This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. 

Three singers and dancers from Harrow who call themselves MITSOTU are doing rather well in a battle of the bands competition at the moment. But, with a £10,000 prize up for grabs, the prospect of playing festivals across the UK and Europe, a tour and a grand final in London’s The O2, Live & Unsigned is a battle of the bands unlike any other.

Holly Cooper, 22, James Collins, 22, and Jimmy Essex, 23, were one of only five acts to make it through the regional finals at the Beck Theatre in Hayes in March to win a place in the area finals in May.

[](https://www.outbrain.com/what-is/default/en)

![Image 4: A 1x1 image, likely be a tacker probe](blob:http://localhost/922ebe887a5b6b01c4cb7a77f1c5301e)

“We got such a great response,” says James, from north Harrow, “the crowd was amazing. And then one of the judges came up to us afterwards and told us we’d got full marks, he said we were outstanding.”

The three friends seamlessly blended together a song of their own, _Won’t Go Down_, and a cover version of Rihanna’s _You Da One_. After hearing they’d made it through, says James, “we were running about screaming, we had so much adrenaline, we’d put so much into it, that we could have gone on and done a whole show!”

Now the band is busy getting ready for the area finals in May, rehearsing every day, writing new music and doing other gigs. The next round will involve another original and another cover – they will be mixing Labrinth’s _Earthqauke_ with the original _Break Your Heart_.

“We’re really excited,” says James, “we just want to get there and do it. Any chance to get in front of a crowd, we love it.”

James and Jimmy met when they were just seven, at Soul Performing Arts School in Ruislip, and went on to the Urdang Academy of performing arts in Finsbury when they were 16, where they met Holly.

They formed their band, whose name is an acronym of the quote ‘music is the soul of the universe', a year and a half ago and have been performing and producing their blend of pop and rock ever since.

They are playing at _Showcase Live_ at Stamford Bridge on Monday, April 16, an industry night with record label talent scouts and producers in attendance that in the past has played host to Jessie J and JLS, and are planning on releasing their own EP later in the year.

There’s no underestimating just how much a win at Live & Unsigned would mean to MITSOTU. “It would be incredible for us.” James says. “This is the dream.”

MITSOTU are playing in the Live & Unsigned regional finals at The Beck Theatre, Grange Road, Hayes in May. The competition is being screened on Sky TV this summer. Details: www.liveandunsigned.uk.com

====================================

[![Image 3: Samuel Nicholls](https://i1.wp.com/www.ayoungertheatre.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/1.jpeg?fit=20%2C20&ssl=1)Samuel Nicholls](https://www.ayoungertheatre.com/author/samuel-nicholls/)December 7, 2020[London](https://www.ayoungertheatre.com/category/london/ "View all posts in London")[Reviews](https://www.ayoungertheatre.com/category/reviews/ "View all posts in Reviews")[Theatre](https://www.ayoungertheatre.com/category/theatre/ "View all posts in Theatre")134 views

Charing Cross Theatre

Review: GHBoy, Charing Cross Theatre

4.0 Overall Score

Pounding music and moody purples flood the stage, drowning out any and all inhibitions. The half-naked young men cut up lines and rip poppers, seeking highs from whatever (and whoever) they can get their hands on. In the cold light of day, their heads will hang heavy with shame and regret – but at night? They pulse with pleasure and relief.

Written by Paul Harvard, _GHBoy_ is a knowing exploration of London’s chemsex community: a hard-partying clique where sex is casual, and drugs are commonplace. Centred around Rob (Jimmy Essex), a stalwart of this queer scene (“I’ve got a handful of poppers and a well-worn jockstrap”), the play examines how trauma is created and smothered by this world of infidelity and substance abuse. We join Rob as he seeks therapy for his self-destructive ways, using art in his meetings to access his subconscious – it’s [Kevin Elyot’s _Coming Clean_](https://www.ayoungertheatre.com/review-coming-clean-trafalgar-studios-2/) by way of [John Logan’s _Red_](https://www.ayoungertheatre.com/review-red-wyndams-theatre/). However, there’s also a wider malevolence at play: an unnamed killer is slashing his way through the chemsex crowd… and how does Rob fit in to it all?

The answer, seemingly, is at the very centre. Under Jon Pashley’s direction, the scenes bleed into one another, slickly intercutting and overlapping – at one point, Rob is reassuring his fiancé, seducing a one-night stand, and confessing to his therapist, all at once. It’s an intense and ambitious narrative flurry, stylised to the extreme, and it’s on the hinges whether or not the audience takes to the character.

Luckily, Rob is a magnificent creation. Like many of his chemsex peers, he’s made up of many ironic layers: he’s a 35-year-old party boy who worries he’s too ‘immature’ for his 20-year-old Catalonian lover; he’s a GHB user, who ‘fights’ his demons by further leaning into their intoxicating ways; and he’s a promise-maker who immediately goes back on his word, admonishing himself as he does so. In as much, Jimmy Essex gives an Atlas-like performance, holding the rest of the play up with his charisma, vulnerability, and grief. Each time he reaches out for sexual validation, or swerves a difficult conversation, it’s heartbreakingly sincere – Rob languishes in his trauma, and we languish with him.

Which is great, because the rest of the play suffers in comparison: everything else seems one-dimensional when put next to Rob…which may be because there is too much going on. As much as the play sets out to examine the realities of the chemsex scene, it also has major detours into systemic homophobia, racism in the post-Grindr gay community, and the role of art in overcoming trauma. This last diversion is also the one that suffers the most – the presence of art is never fully justified within the larger play, either thematically or narratively; when Rob plays with his paints, it may be nice for him, but it’s a confusing digression for the audience.

GHBoy _is running at the Charing Cross Theatre until 20th December_._For more information and tickets, see the[Charing Cross Theatre website](https://charingcrosstheatre.co.uk/theatre/ghboy)._

 This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. 

Former Hollyoaks actor Jimmy Essex has revealed he is engaged to his boyfriend of six years.

The soap star, who played Adam Donovan in the Channel 4 show, was proposed to during a holiday in Sri Lanka by his musician partner Charles.

Essex, 30, shared a picture to Instagram showing him and his boyfriend kissing while he held a diamond ring up to the camera.

[](https://www.outbrain.com/what-is/default/en)

The post was captioned: “So … this happened.” Essex added a diamond ring emoji.

Earlier, Charles shared a series of pictures to Instagram showing the couple, both dressed in white, embracing.

Alongside the images, he wrote: “6 years and counting… He said yes.” Essex’s Hollyoaks co-star Tamara Wall commented on his post: “Best thing ever!!!!!!!”

Blue singer and former Hollyoaks star Duncan James wrote: “Awwwww massive congrats guys.”

Essex’s character was killed off last year.

=====

“Underpowered and overstuffed”

[Reviews](https://www.thestage.co.uk/reviews/reviews)Dec 7, 2020[by Paul Vale](https://www.thestage.co.uk/author-paul-vale "Paul Vale")Charing Cross Theatre, London

[![Image 19: Jimmy Essex in GHBoy at Charing Cross Theatre, London. Photo: Bettina John](https://d3s3zh7icgjwgd.cloudfront.net/AcuCustom/Sitename/DAM/200/Jimmy-Essex-Robert-Finch_Standard.-Credit-Bettina-John.jpg)](https://d3s3zh7icgjwgd.cloudfront.net/AcuCustom/Sitename/DAM/200/Jimmy-Essex-Robert-Finch_Standard.-Credit-Bettina-John.jpg)

Jimmy Essex in GHBoy at Charing Cross Theatre, London. Photo: Bettina John

Well-meaning but stilted new play that lacks dramatic focus

[![Image 20: Facebook](https://d3s3zh7icgjwgd.cloudfront.net/AcuCustom/Sitename/Icon/Icons/19tsFBIcon.svg)](http://www.facebook.com/share.php?u=https://www.thestage.co.uk/reviews/ghboy&t=GHBoy)[![Image 21: Twitter](https://d3s3zh7icgjwgd.cloudfront.net/AcuCustom/Sitename/Icon/Icons/X_logo.jpg)](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=https://www.thestage.co.uk/reviews/ghboy&title=GHBoy)[![Image 22: LinkedIn](https://d3s3zh7icgjwgd.cloudfront.net/AcuCustom/Sitename/Icon/Icons/17tsLinkedInIcon.svg)](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.thestage.co.uk%2Freviews%2Fghboy&text=GHBoy)

Between 2014 and 2015, serial killer and rapist Stephen Port murdered at least four men after administering an overdose of the drug GHB. A sluggish investigation failed to connect the victims to Port, leading critics to suggest that the police had failed to recognise the deaths as anything other than casual drug misuse. It’s this revelation that prompted tyro playwright Paul Harvard to tackle the sensitive and thorny issue of recreational drug use within the gay community.

Robert is an addict seeking therapy while mourning the recent death of his father. A surprise proposal from his new boyfriend amplifies his paranoia but eventually he makes a breakthrough and begins to address the shadows in his past. GHBoy unfolds as a linear narrative, bookended with art therapy sessions that help Robert unlock the events of his addiction.

Several playwrights have already explored this issue with varying degrees of success, but Harvard’s work seems both underpowered and overstuffed. The author’s written style is immediate but lacks consistent dramatic structure, with peripheral characters underwritten and a protagonist who seems defined primarily by who he sleeps with and the drugs he takes.

Jon Pashley’ s oddly stilted direction seems ill-suited both to the subject matter and the space, which can’t decide if it’s traverse or thrust. Jimmy Essex does a good job of bringing this tortured character to life, capturing the physical restlessness of a soul in crisis.

Postponed from production earlier in the year, Harvard’s play might benefit from further workshops and more fluid direction.

[](whatsapp://send?text=X%20Factor%E2%80%99s%20Mitsotu%3A%20It%E2%80%99s%20a%20sex%20and%20booze%20fuelled%20party%20behind%20the%20scenes%20https%3A%2F%2Fmetro.co.uk%2F2012%2F09%2F26%2Fx-factors-mitsotu-its-a-sex-and-booze-fuelled-party-behind-the-scenes-586152%2F%3Fito%3Darticle.desktop.share.top.whatsapp)[](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https%3A%2F%2Fmetro.co.uk%2F2012%2F09%2F26%2Fx-factors-mitsotu-its-a-sex-and-booze-fuelled-party-behind-the-scenes-586152%2F%3Fito%3Darticle.desktop.share.top.twitter&text=X%20Factor%26%238217%3Bs%20Mitsotu%3A%20It%26%238217%3Bs%20a%20sex%20and%20booze%20fuelled%20party%20behind%20the%20scenes&via=MetroUK)[](https://metro.co.uk/2012/09/26/x-factors-mitsotu-its-a-sex-and-booze-fuelled-party-behind-the-scenes-586152/)Link is copied[](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fmetro.co.uk%2F2012%2F09%2F26%2Fx-factors-mitsotu-its-a-sex-and-booze-fuelled-party-behind-the-scenes-586152%2F%3Fito%3Darticle.desktop.share.top.facebook) [Comments](https://metro.co.uk/2012/09/26/x-factors-mitsotu-its-a-sex-and-booze-fuelled-party-behind-the-scenes-586152/#metro-comments-container)

Exclusive: The X Factor’s squeaky clean new look might be proving a turn-off for viewers but behind the scenes it’s a sex and booze fuelled party, says groups hopeful Mitsotu.

![Image 1: Mitsotu](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2012/09/article-1348675600445-1537feaa000005dc-34775_636x421.jpg)

Mitsotu Picture Caption: The multi BAFTA-award winning entertainment show returns to our screens for an explosive ninth series. This year’s exciting new judging panel will hit the road and travel the length and breadth of Britain for live auditions with potential singers. Dermot O’Leary returns to host the proceedings on ITV1 and will be on hand to celebrate with the successful acts and mop up the tears of those who aren’t. And ITV2’s Xtra Factor will be bringing viewers all the behind the scenes gossip, exclusive interviews with the judges and unforgettable auditions that will make you cry with laughter and cheer on the stars of tomorrow. Photographer: Ken McKay Copyright: THAMES TV/SYCO

Contestants were left to party hard during the bootcamp stages of the ITV show, Mitsotu  singer James Collins told me in an exclusive interview.

‘People were running down corridors naked,’ he said. ‘It was crazy. People were hooking up everywhere.

‘Everyone was trying to show off their X Factor in all senses.’

James, from Harrow, north-west London, was shocked strict rules normally    associated with Simon Cowell’s show had gone out of the window. ‘We set our own rules,’ he said of the bootcamp orgies at Liverpool’s Jury’s Inn hotel.

![Image 2: Sharon Osbourne, Louis Walsh](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2012/09/article-1348676348009-0b6ef2dd000005dc-819650_466x310.jpg)

Sharon Osbourne joined Louis Walsh in Las Vegas to decide which groups would go through to the live shows (Picture: ITV)

But he revealed the show’s bosses ordered an end to the boozing and bonking when the contest moved to the judge’s house phase in Las Vegas.  Prince Harry’s naked shenanigans in Sin City prompted judge Louis Walsh to order a curfew to rein in contestants’ bad behaviour.

‘There was a “Prince Harry warning”,’ said James, 22. ‘Louis told us not to party.’ As for his bandmates – Holly Cooper and Jimmy Essex, both, 23 – James said they went on the show because ‘we needed a big break.’

‘We’ve all had careers. I’ve danced on Janet Jackson’s tour,’ he said.

And the band’s name? It’s an acronym of the pals’ tattoos, which read: ‘Music is the soul of the universe,’ he said.

Hollyoaks star Jimmy Essex gets engaged to boyfriend of six years
=================================================================

He shared the news on Instagram.

![Image 3: Hollyoaks actor Jimmy Essex has revealed he is engaged to his boyfriend of six years (Matt Crossick/PA Wire)](https://focus.independent.ie/thumbor/Fdvx5aB_sAKQJAIfOa2pmxAWuFg=/0x14:2667x1485/960x640/prod-mh-ireland/6875b3f6-c2b1-11ed-95ea-0210609a3fe2)

Hollyoaks actor Jimmy Essex has revealed he is engaged to his boyfriend of six years (Matt Crossick/PA Wire)

By Keiran Southern, Press Association Los Angeles Correspondent

Mon 21 Jan 2019 at 22:14

Former Hollyoaks actor Jimmy Essex has revealed he is engaged to his boyfriend of six years.

The soap star, who played Adam Donovan in the Channel 4 show, was proposed to during a holiday in Sri Lanka by his musician partner Charles.

Essex, 30, shared a picture to Instagram showing him and his boyfriend kissing while he held a diamond ring up to the camera.

The post was captioned: “So … this happened.” Essex added a diamond ring emoji.

Earlier, Charles shared a series of pictures to Instagram showing the couple, both dressed in white, embracing.

Alongside the images, he wrote: “6  years and counting… He said yes.” Essex’s Hollyoaks co-star Tamara Wall commented on his post: “Best thing ever!!!!!!!”

Blue singer and former Hollyoaks star Duncan James wrote: “Awwwww massive congrats guys.”

Essex’s character was killed off last year.
